subject: paired-exchange-42 InterGen research canonical clip
review_scope: Independent review of 24-frame contact sheets from full 120-frame WebGL captures, plus every saved canonical joint frame; the main agent must watch the full video for final visual verification.
decision: Conditional research demonstration only; do not present as native Core, verified contact, or a finished martial-arts performance.

visual_findings.exchange: Corrected capture shows two performers in close partner range, a mutual arm exchange around 1.5–3.9 s, and a coordinated step apart. This is materially more connected than the earlier far-apart duet. The motion reads as a compact block/shove or scuffle; a separate sidestep dodge and decisive controlled push are not clearly readable.
timing_observable_in_sampled_frames: 0.0–1.3 s: near each other with guarded or preparatory arm movements; little dramatic action.
1.55–3.9 s: approach, crossed forearms, close block/shove-like partner exchange; apparent proximity varies and no stable hand-to-hand hold is visible.
4.15–5.95 s: disengage and widen their spacing; blue actor ends leaning with bent arms, a weak final pose.
visual_findings.render_fitting_comparison: The first paired retarget capture visibly raised/bent arms unnaturally at rest. The corrected capture's shared root-height adjustment resolves that specific regression while preserving the same underlying canonical motion. The baseline fitting shows more natural rest but does not preserve native world wrists.
visual_findings.body_overlap: Torso centers remain separate in joint data; a hand/forearm joint-center pair reaches 0.017 m at frame 61, so limb mesh intersection remains possible. The sheet cannot establish collision-free mesh contact.
visual_findings.feet_and_scene: Actors remain on the generated city street backdrop in sampled frames. Some light foot lift or sliding is visually plausible; no foot-plant or mesh-ground claim follows from this review. The city is a rendering backdrop, not scene-conditioned generation.
visual_findings.high_five_baseline: Reject as high-five preset: sampled frames show approach and prolonged low hand/forearm meeting, without a crisp overhead palm strike and release.
visual_findings.dance_paired: Corrected capture preserves a recognizable shared hold and turn around 2.8–4.0 s without the earlier root-height wrist regression. The first roughly two seconds remain static with palms raised; the result is a small partnered turn, not a rich dance sequence.

all_joint_center_gap_m.interpretation: A joint-center proxy, not a mesh collision test.

closest_cross_wrist_gap_m.interpretation: No sustained hand contact or explicit contact timing.

canonical_measurements.interpretation: The new paired sample is substantially closer and has smaller frame-to-frame joint jumps. These values support continuity and proximity, not semantic quality or physical interaction.

retarget_provenance.source: InterGen paired research model, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 checkpoint; service retargeted SMPL22 at 30 fps to Core27 at 20 fps.
retarget_provenance.qualification: Wrist fitting accurately retains the source gap; it does not close that gap or enforce hand contact, foot locks, or mesh collision avoidance.

next_review_gate: Main agent watches full corrected video, especially frames 25–80 and 85–119, and decides whether the short block/shove exchange is a useful labeled research preset. Reject any claim that it satisfies the full dodge–block–push prompt or can be shipped as the native motion workflow.

additional_trial.name: paired-boxing-7303
additional_trial.decision: Reject full 6-second clip as a default preset because the ending intersects the actors. Its earlier punches/ducks are a stronger action direction than the exchange.
sampled_visual_timing: 0–1.3 s: broad punching/guarding gestures, with blue ducking around 0.8–1.1 s; some actions read as independent rather than clearly causally linked.
1.55–2.35 s: green passes in front of blue. This apparent screen overlap is mostly camera occlusion rather than torso-centerline collision in the saved joints.
2.85–3.35 s: blue ducks low as green crosses close; readable second evasion but body clearance is borderline.
5.4–5.95 s: performers converge and finish visibly interpenetrating back to back; fails full-sequence acceptance.

all_joint_center_gap_m.interpretation: Joint centers are only a proxy, but high-resolution last frame independently shows body intersection.

additional_trial.recommendation: Keep as failed full-trial provenance. A separately labeled early excerpt could be useful for research review, but the source is still the full generated sequence and no corrected partner-collision result has been demonstrated.

boxing_7304_trial.decision: Reject as a convincing full boxing default. It passes the specified torso joint-center spacing screen that boxing-7303 failed, but the latter half loses two-person action readability.
sampled_visual_findings: 0.5–2.4 s: facing sparring, ducking, and crossing arm motion are visible; some action is plausible but no exact punch-contact timing is established.
2.6–3.9 s: one actor turns and crosses in front of the other, with long camera occlusion; the requested role switch is not clearly readable.
5.45–5.95 s: they converge again; the last frame shows heads nearly touching and little posed resolution. It does not have the gross torso intersection seen in boxing-7303.

all_joint_center_gap_m.interpretation: Limb proximity remains; no mesh collision verification.

boxing_7304_trial.comparison: Better gross body clearance than boxing-7303, less coherent partner exchange than exchange-42 corrected. The original 7303 failure remains documented in additional_trial.
